newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canada's Bombardier announces AMR jet order.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Bombardier announces AMR jet order.

text.p: Canadian aircraft manufacturer Bombardier unveiled an order on Tuesday from domestic U.S. airline American Eagle for up to 50 of its Canadair regional passenger jets.

The order, from part of the AMR Corp airlines giant, is for 25 of the Canadair's new 70-seat version with an option for 25 more aircraft, Bombardier Aerospace President Robert Brown said at the Paris air show. The order makes American the launch customer for the larger 70-seat version, with the previous version built to fly up to 50 passengers.
No financial details were immediately available.
The order was the second deal involving expansion of American Eagle's regional fleet announced in Paris on Tuesday.

The domestic U.S. carrier earlier announced a billion dollar order for up to 67 short-range passenger jets from Brazilian manufacturer Embraer. It said it was buying 42 50-seat EMB-145 regional jets and taking options on a further 25 aircraft. American said the firm orders alone were worth $700 million.
American Eagle senior vice president Peter Pappas said it had decided to buy the new fleet following a succesful rationalisation of its operations last year.
